summary:
Please excuse the dim ribbon and the typoz; I’m very tired as is Tessa taking care of Christopher. He seems to feel that being up all night talking is good and being put in his cradle and left alone is bad. He is growing by leaps and bounds— well over ten pounds now, and his appetite cannot be compared to anything in this century. We firmly expect him to devour the cat Pinky and then ask, “So what else do I get?” 

We had bad car trouble—the whole transmission went out, then the front end, then the starter motor, then we had to buy four new tires, and last but not least the choke settled into one position (i.e. closed). But we got it all fixed, whereupon our color TV went out, costing us $209. But the car works fine now and my confidence in it is returning (but only slowly). 

The magazine (slick) Vertex interviewed me for one and a half hours; out of that the interviewer extracted about 4,000 words which make me sound really great. They will be by one day soon to photograph me for the interview. And a French girl who interviewed Toynbee and Buckmeister Fuller is fly­ ing here to interview me for Paris TV. I sense intrigue. I also sense Tessa beating me to death with Christopher as the bat.
